summary: DESIGN-001 is implementable and its contract (preconditions, postconditions, errors, boundaries) is precise. The integer-arithmetic rank -(-p*N//100) is correct, and the expected values of TEST-001..016 recompute correctly. Unit tests detect the targeted defects (TEST-010 ceil vs floor/round, TEST-011 float error) and the system tests cover AC-001-1..6 and AC-002-1..3. Only minor remarks remain.

checklist.note: Signature, algorithm and 0-based index r-1 are unambiguous.
ValueError conditions (bool/float/str/range/empty) and the 1, 100, N=1 and exact-multiple boundaries are stated.

checklist.item: Unit tests can detect contract violations
checklist.note: Normal, abnormal and boundary tests have concrete expected values; TEST-010 and TEST-011 target rounding defects; TEST-003 detects in-place sort.
Single component, no interfaces; justified in the architecture.

checklist.item: System specs cover every acceptance criterion
checklist.note: TEST-013 covers AC-001-1..5, TEST-014 covers AC-001-6, TEST-015 covers AC-002-1..3, TEST-016 covers REQ-003.

checklist.item: Nothing designed that no requirement asks for

findings.description: TEST-012 uses 80 -> 5 in [1,5,5,5,9]. Ranks 2, 3 and 4 all give 5, so an off-by-one in the rank cannot be detected. Use duplicate values that are distinguishable at the neighbouring ranks, or add a case where an off-by-one changes the result.

The behaviour for NaN in scores is undefined (ASM-002 only excludes non-numeric types), and so is the behaviour for a non-ValueError failure on a non-iterable scores argument. This is acceptable as an assumption but not stated in the design contract.

The decision to reject p=50.0 (a float with an integral value) follows REQ-002 (non-integer value) and is tested in TEST-005, but it is not an explicit acceptance criterion. It is consistent across the requirements, design and tests.
